questions.q: Why should an integration use a dedicated service account instead of an employee's personal login?
options: Personal logins are always more secure
A dedicated account survives staff turnover and is clearly identifiable in a security review
Oracle Fusion technically forbids personal logins from ever working
There is no real difference
questions.explain: A dedicated integration user avoids breaking when an employee leaves and is easier to audit.

questions.q: What does "least privilege" mean when applied to an integration user?
options: Granting the broadest possible access to avoid future requests
Giving the integration user no access at all
Granting only the specific roles, business units, and access level the integration actually needs
Letting every integration share one superuser account
questions.explain: Least privilege means scoping access narrowly to actual need.

questions.q: An integration only ever reads AR data and never writes to it. Under least privilege, what access should its user have?
options: Full read/write access to all business units
No access, since reading isn't necessary
Administrative access to all Fusion modules
Read-only access scoped to the AR data it actually needs
questions.explain: Read-only, narrowly scoped access matches what the integration actually requires.

questions.q: What is a concrete risk of using a personal employee login for an integration?
options: The integration will run faster
The integration breaks if that employee's password is reset or they leave the company
JSON responses will stop working
There is no risk at all
questions.explain: A personal-login dependency breaks when that individual's account changes.

questions.q: Who should typically own the lifecycle (rotation, review, deactivation) of an integration user's credentials?
options: No one — it should never be reviewed
Whichever employee first set it up, indefinitely
IT/security, as a managed process, not one individual employee
The external vendor's support team exclusively
questions.explain: Centralized ownership by IT/security avoids dependency on a single person.
